title: What If You Could See With Sound Like a Bat? You Can Learn in 10 Weeks

scenes.text: What if you could see with sound, like a bat? Some blind people do. You could learn.
Daniel Kish lost his eyes as a baby. He clicks his tongue, reads the echoes, and rides a mountain bike.
In 2011, scanners showed the echoes lighting up his visual cortex, the part of the brain sighted people see with.
In 2021, Durham University trained 12 blind and 14 sighted people, some aged 79, for ten weeks.
By the end they steered through virtual mazes almost as well as expert echolocators. Sighted trainees sometimes did best.
Three months on, 10 of the 12 blind trainees said they lived more independently. The ability was there all along.

In 2021, Durham University trained 12 blind and 14 sighted people aged 21 to 79 for ten weeks, and they steered virtual mazes nearly as well as experts (PLOS ONE).
Three months later, 10 of the 12 blind participants reported more independence.
